liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Looks Like Rain** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Harmonies are fantastic, and steel guitar suits Bobby's song; reviewer urges listening to this track; Reviewer calls it a unique, early version of the song [2][10][12][15]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Short for the period but psychedelic, in the reviewer's view; Reviewer calls it particularly hot as the band finds its speed [5][13]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Reviewer says Donna's singing mars this song and Playing In The Band [12]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer finds it nice but a bit mellow, with vocals lacking [6]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Described as rollicking [5]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Reviewer calls it amazing [14]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Truckin' into The Other One is intense and surreal, with the jam building momentum [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.jackson.smith.94377.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 216 min; rated 4.38/5 by 16 [1]
- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.thecore.4640.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 195 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Splices, clipped song openings, a brief dropout, and frequent distortion from Keith's piano on loud notes [2]
- **gd72-04-11.sbd.giles.12186.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 195 min; rated 4.1/5 by 21 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the board lower in quality than the pristine European soundboards, though the music rates higher; Listening to only Bobby's guitar channel reveals why the band sounded different after 1974, per the reviewer; Acknowledged muddiness, but extremely listenable [5][11][12][14][15]

## Around the show

- Reviewer hears Phil singing harmonies and a bittersweet slide from Jerry, while the vocals are poor [7]
- Reviewer disputes the heroin explanation for weak vocals, saying Garcia did not start using until early 1977 [8]
- Reviewer says this show outshines nearly everything else from 1972 [11]
- Reviewer ranks this Other One among the tour's best, a cross between the Wigan and Amsterdam versions [13]
- Reviewer contrasts it with 1977 shows, saying there is no shuffle-style Sugar Magnolia here [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.jackson.smith.94377.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rex Jackson; transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > Master Reel [1]
- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.thecore.4640.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>D>CD [2]. Also: Uploader used Sound Forge to edit blemishes, adjust levels and reduce distortion [2]
- **gd72-04-11.sbd.giles.12186.sbeok.shnf**: source: remastered by Bill Giles - source is SBD MC>D>CD>SoundForge>CDSee info file for flaws & Bill's mastering notes [3]. Also: Brokedown Palace from this show appears on the official release Steppin' Out, in pristine sound; Remastered by Bill Giles from a soundboard master cassette, via digital, CD and SoundForge, to CD [3][15]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Exclusive April 11, 1972 Download](https://www.dead.net/features/exclusive-april-11-1972-download) [19]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 4/11/72 Newcastle City Hall, N…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26793055741/) [20]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26793055741/) [21]
